nodeData.topic: Constitution of Kenya 2010 — article by article · draft
nodeData.note: Draft · review in progress. First draft, not yet reviewed by a lawyer. Do not rely on it for exams, court or advice. One map per chapter of the Constitution, one bubble per Article in plain words, each linked to the official text on the Kenya Law Reform Commission site (klrc.go.ke). Chapters 1–4 (Articles 1–59) so far; a new chapter is added every Friday. Search words: Katiba, Constitution of Kenya 2010, Bill of Rights, Article, Ibara.

No torture, no slavery, fair trial, habeas corpus — never limited.
Citizens may access State-held information and information needed to protect a right.
Told why, may stay silent, advocate, court within 24 hours, bail unless compelling reasons.
Peaceably and unarmed.

children.topic: Bill of Rights, who it binds (Art. 20)
children.note: All law, all State organs and all persons, including private persons.
Name, education, basics, protection, both parents; best interests paramount.
Either parent a citizen on the day of birth; foundlings under eight presumed citizens.
Seven years married to a citizen, or seven years lawful residence, or adoption.
Protected for present and future generations.
Quality, information, safety and economic interests, compensation.
47 counties in the First Schedule; two distinct, inter-dependent levels of government.
Culture as the foundation of the nation; royalties to communities; indigenous seeds.
Everyone must respect, uphold and defend it; an unconstitutional government is unlawful.
A citizen by birth keeps Kenyan citizenship on taking another.
Health, housing, food, water, social security, education; no denial of emergency treatment.
Nobody may be denied emergency medical treatment.
No discrimination; affirmative action; no more than two-thirds of a body of one gender.
Expeditious, efficient, lawful, reasonable, procedurally fair; written reasons.
Presumption of innocence, disclosure, interpreter, no double jeopardy, appeal; tainted evidence excluded.
Adults of the opposite sex, free consent, equal rights in and after marriage.
Excludes war propaganda, incitement, hate speech and advocacy of hatred.
Two-thirds rule for Parliament to be realised progressively, legislation by 27 August 2015.
A detained person may ask the court to test the detention; the right can never be limited.
Promotes and monitors human rights; anyone may complain; now split into KNCHR, NGEC and the Ombudsman.
Swahili for Constitution / Article — this library.
Fair pay, reasonable conditions, trade unions, the right to strike, collective bargaining.
Kiswahili is the national language; Kiswahili and English are official.
Only by law, reasonable and justifiable in an open and democratic society; five factors; State proves it.
No State control or penalties; independent licensing and standards body.
Affirmative action, representation, water, health and infrastructure.
Madaraka 1 June, Mashujaa 20 October, Jamhuri 12 December.
Patriotism, rule of law, participation, dignity, equity, integrity, transparency, accountability, sustainable development.
Kenya has no official religion.
Participation, dignity, care from family and State.
Every citizen is entitled to a passport; it can be withheld only under an Act meeting Article 24.
Dignity, access, Sign language and Braille; at least five per cent in public bodies.
Free, fair and regular elections; every adult citizen may register, vote and stand.
Person, home, property, possessions, private information, communications.
Own property anywhere; compulsory acquisition only for a public purpose with prompt, full, just compensation.
Declaration, injunction, conservatory order, invalidity, compensation, judicial review.
Kenya is a sovereign, multi-party democratic Republic.
Only registered citizens and presumed foundlings; fraud, war, serious crime.
Life begins at conception; abortion only for emergency treatment or danger to the mother, or under another written law.
All State power belongs to the people and is used only under the Constitution, directly or through elected representatives.
Anyone may sue, also for others, a group or the public interest; no filing fee.
14 days, extensions by the National Assembly, Supreme Court review.
The highest law; conflicting law is void to the extent of the clash; ratified treaties are part of Kenyan law.
Education, participation, employment, protection.
